definitions.explanation: The quality of refusing to give in despite difficulties, opposition, or hardship. Used as a noun or as a の-modifier.

examples.japanese: {不屈|ふくつ}の{精神|せいしん}で{戦|たたか}う。
examples.english: To fight with an indomitable spirit.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{不屈|ふくつ}の{意志|いし}で{病気|びょうき}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: She overcame her illness with unyielding willpower.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{失敗|しっぱい}しても{諦|あきら}めない{不屈|ふくつ}の{姿勢|しせい}が、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{感動|かんどう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: The indomitable attitude of never giving up despite repeated failures moved many people.

notes:
A compound of {不|ふ} (not) and {屈|くつ} (yield, bend). Literally "not yielding." Almost always used as a の-modifier before abstract nouns like {精神|せいしん}, {意志|いし}, or {闘志|とうし}.

USAGE:
Rarely used alone as a standalone noun; it almost always modifies another word. The phrase {不屈|ふくつ}の{精神|せいしん} (indomitable spirit) is particularly common and iconic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不屈|ふくつ}の{精神|せいしん} — indomitable spirit
- {不屈|ふくつ}の{意志|いし} — unyielding will
- {不屈|ふくつ}の{闘志|とうし} — dauntless fighting spirit
- {不屈|ふくつ}の{努力|どりょく} — relentless effort

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頑強|がんきょう} — tenacious, stubborn (strong resistance)
- {粘|ねば}り{強|づよ}い — tenacious, persistent (sustained effort)
- {不撓不屈|ふとうふくつ} — indomitable and unbending (four-character compound, more literary)
